memories.content: HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess the reproducibility of results if the prototype version used in the evaluation is not disclosed.
Record the manipulated and fixed elements of compared design alternatives so that other researchers can reconstruct them.
Records of formative evaluation decisions enable the reconstruction of connections between raw data, interpretation, and design modifications.
The user must make it possible to trace which observations each prototype version reflects so the process of deriving design knowledge can be reviewed.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate aspects of HCI research rigor. The reference frame focuses on reconstructing prototypes, alternatives, and formative design lineage, while the compared frame covers proposal answerability, preregistration, target planning, field operations, safety, and contribution framing. No direct cross-frame correspondence is established.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-side requirement about identifying the evaluated artifact; the compared frame contains no matching claim.
relations.summary: Evaluations should disclose the prototype version used so reviewers can assess reproducibility.

relations.reason: This reference-side requirement concerns controlled differences among design alternatives and has no operational counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Compared design alternatives should document manipulated and fixed elements to support reconstruction.

relations.reason: The reference memories split one provenance requirement between decision-chain records and mappings from observations to prototype versions; the compared frame does not address iterative design lineage.
relations.summary: Formative records should preserve traceable lineage from observations and raw data through interpretation and decisions to prototype modifications.

relations.reason: The compared memories state the same one-sided answerability requirement as an authoring instruction and a reviewer judgment criterion; the reference frame does not address research-question mappings.
relations.summary: Each HCI research question should be traceable to its field or user data sources and analysis procedures.

relations.reason: This compared-side governance requirement is independently useful and is not addressed by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should specify criteria for judging changes to the plan.

relations.reason: This compared-side record-location requirement is distinct from change criteria and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should specify where changes to the plan will be recorded.

relations.reason: These compared memories split one target-bound policy across the overall requirement, reviewer rationale, minimum deliverable, session and facilitator implications, and maximum deliverable; the reference frame contains no target-planning claim.
relations.summary: A minimum-to-maximum target range should give each bound a justified and operationally different consequence for deliverables, workload, schedule, or cost.

relations.reason: The compared memories express the rationale and uncertainty tradeoff of using a bounded range; the reference frame does not address uncertain targets.
relations.summary: A bounded target range can represent expected confirmation uncertainty more honestly than a guaranteed fixed estimate.

relations.reason: This compared-side specification concerns data-collection instruments and has no matching reference-side requirement.
relations.summary: Proposals should identify the records, logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.

relations.reason: This compared-side specification concerns collection timing and is independently useful from instrument selection; the reference frame does not address it.
relations.summary: Proposals should state whether each type of field and user data is collected before, during, or after deployment.

relations.reason: This compared-side attribution claim introduces environmental failure causes absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field-deployment task failures may arise independently from network or service instability as well as design choices.

relations.reason: This compared-side contingency policy governs safety escalation and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: When a field-system safety signal occurs, institutional safety procedures take precedence over research scheduling and data collection.

relations.reason: This compared-side observation concerns contribution framing rather than reproducibility documentation and is absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely addresses research-question answerability, preregistration changes, data-collection specifications, uncertainty-aware target ranges, deployment failures and safety, and the framing of design contributions.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely emphasizes disclosing evaluated prototype versions, reconstructing design alternatives, and tracing observations and formative decisions into design changes.
